messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected for route `streaming.generate` (region: us-west-2). p95=2.6s, p99=12.1s, error-rate 0.6% — paging @eng-sre, incident: INC-3690012345

eng-sre-maya: taking this ticket. I'm pulling dashboards now, can someone paste the affected node list?

sre-alex: looks like high tail on a subset of nodes in pool gpu-shared-2. p95 jump started ~2026-11-03T04:12Z, correlates with high block_io wait on those hosts.

eng-runtime-ryan: we see increased write_iops from tenant 'geo-vector' spikes at 04:10Z. NVME latency also elevated. suspect noisy neighbor causing cgroup IO thrashing.

ops-jen: confirmed. `iostat -x` on node gpu-22 shows %util 99, await 45ms. nvme stats show many small writes.

eng-sre-maya: quick customer-impact summary for ops/cs: multiple customers saw streaming stalls and reconnects; CS flagged AcmeMaps and TourPro as reporting slow responses (timeouts ~10s). Not a full outage but SLO breach for latency.

cs-luis: on AcmeMaps call now, they saw many stream stalls and some dropped events. They are asking for ETA and whether we can migrate them briefly.

eng-runtime-ryan: mitigation options: 1) apply per-cgroup io.max caps on noisy cgroups; 2) evict/migrate offending pods to dedicated pool; 3) throttle tenant at router (rate-limit/burst) while we mitigate.

eng-sre-maya: doing mitigation 1 first — applying IO cap to the top offending cgroup for tenant `geo-vector`. Command I'm going to run on node gpu-22:```bash
# identify cgroup
cat /proc/$(pgrep -f "pod:geo-vector")/cgroup
# set io cap (cgroup v2)
echo "8:0 rbps=104857600 wbps=52428800" > /sys/fs/cgroup/unified/<cgroup-path>/io.max
```

sre-alex: note: exact path varies by runtime; if using systemd slice you'll need to map pod -> slice. I'll assist on node.

ops-jen: i'm on node gpu-22 via bastion. confirm run when ready.

eng-sre-maya: applied a conservative cap (rbps=100MB/s wbps=50MB/s) to geo-vector cgroup on gpu-22 at 04:21Z.

incident-bot: [STATUS] mitigation action recorded: io.cap applied to cgroup `kubepods.slice/pod.../geo-vector` by eng-sre-maya at 3690012060

eng-runtime-ryan: initial impact: p99 for streaming fell from 12.1s -> ~6.0s within 90s. p95 back under 1.2s for the node we patched. Good signal.

cs-luis: AcmeMaps reports fewer stalls but still seeing occasional 6-7s tails. They want guaranteed no disruption.

eng-sre-maya: next step: migrate geo-vector pods off shared pool to dedicated pool (dedicated-gpu-geo) to fully isolate. Planning: scale-up dedicated pool + drain pods.

ops-jen: preparing to provision dedicated nodes. running helm job to spin up 2 nodes in dedicated-gpu-geo. ETA ~6-8 minutes.

sre-alex: while nodes spin, adding temporary router-level fallback for most critical customers to model-variant `streaming-lite` (lower throughput, more CPU-friendly) — should reduce GPU IO bursts. Patch command:```json
{
  "route": "streaming.generate",
  "fallback_rule": {
    "match_customers": ["AcmeMaps"],
    "model_variant": "streaming-lite",
    "duration": "15m"
  }
}
```

eng-runtime-ryan: applied fallback for AcmeMaps at 04:30Z. Traffic shows immediate reduction in GPU-bound requests.

incident-bot: [UPDATE] p95=1.1s, p99=3.4s (cluster-wide) after router fallback and io cap. Still monitoring.

cs-luis: relaying to AcmeMaps — ETA for no-customer-impact is ~15m if migration succeeds. They asked for postmortem and steps we took.

eng-sre-maya: migration complete: geo-vector pods cordoned + drained from gpu-22 -> dedicated-gpu-geo at 04:38Z. Verified pods running on dedicated nodes.

ops-jen: dedicated nodes healthy. nvme metrics on gpu-22 back to baseline %util 12.

incident-bot: [RESOLVE CHECK] p95=0.95s, p99=1.8s, error-rate 0.1%. No further streaming stalls observed in last 5m. Recommend transitioning to post-incident review.

eng-sre-maya: taking lead for postmortem. Preliminary root cause: tenant `geo-vector` issued sustained small-write NVME IO causing host-level queue saturation; cgroup/io.max not previously tuned for this workload; multi-tenant pool lacked IO isolation knobs by default. Action items: (A) default io.max profiles for shared pools, (B) autoscale dedicated pools faster for IO-heavy tenants, (C) router-level soft-fallback when per-tenant IO alarms trigger, (D) add p99 streaming runbooks and test drills.

sre-alex: I'll file the follow-up tickets and schedule a blameless postmortem. tagging eng-runtime and infra for kernel/cgroup tuning.

cs-luis: AcmeMaps very appreciative of quick mitigation. need a summary email — I'll draft.

eng-sre-maya: handoff: ops-jen will monitor next 2 hours, I'm moving to postmortem doc. If any regression, page @oncall-rotation.

ops-jen: monitoring now. @eng-sre-maya, I'll ping if anything trends up.

incident-bot: [INCIDENT CLOSED] INC-3690012345 closed by eng-sre-maya at 3690013200 — duration 11m.

sre-alex: thanks everyone. short retro scheduled for tomorrow.

eng-runtime-ryan: quick note for runbook: add `tc qdisc` vs cgroup io.max comparison appendix — we hit path choices mid-incident which slowed mitigations.

eng-sre-maya: good point. adding to action items.

cs-luis: sending customer note now.

sre-alex: closing thread. great response team work :thumbsup:
